title: Improve dedicated autoscaler: priority burst throughput guarantees + utilization reporting
author: Jordan Lee
description: Motivation: several customers running Dedicated fleets reported occasional transient throughput drops during multi-tenant bursts and asked for stronger throughput guarantees for priority classes while preserving overall utilization reporting. This change introduces a priority-aware burst throughput guarantee layer in the dedicated autoscaler and expands utilization reporting to include per-priority token throughput, burst headroom, and queueing latency histograms. Design summary: add a priority token-bucket overlay that can reserve short-term burst capacity for business-critical classes, implement a per-fleet headroom tracker that emits metrics for guaranteed vs available throughput, and extend the existing utilization reporter to surface priority breakdowns and queue latency percentiles. Backwards compatibility: behavior is opt-in per-fleet via a new autoscaler config block (priority_burst: enabled:true | false, reserve_ms:int, max_burst_tokens:int) so existing fleets see no change unless enabled. Rollout: staged rollout with config flag enabled for internal test fleets then a canary on a small customer fleet; safety net uses existing fallback to best-effort routing when guarantees cannot be satisfied. Testing: unit tests for token-bucket logic, integration tests for autoscaler interactions, end-to-end perf runs comparing baseline and with guarantees enabled. Impact: reduces observed tail queueing for priority requests during high contention while preserving global throughput accounting and improving observability for capacity planning.

review_thread: Priya Patel: Nice approach. Can you clarify how reservation interacts with existing burst tokens when a high-priority request arrives?

Jordan Lee: Reservation consumes from the priority token-bucket first; if reservation is depleted we fall back to normal fleet token-bucket and best-effort routing. Added a diagram and explanation in controller.go comment.
Ethan Kim: Please ensure we have telemetry that clearly distinguishes reserved vs consumed tokens for billing and debugging.
Jordan Lee: Added separate counters and a headroom gauge for reserved tokens. See runtime headroom_tracker.go changes and observability migration file.
Maria Gonzales: Minor nit: config validation should reject reserve_ms <=0 and warn if max_burst_tokens > fleet_capacity. Also add a migration note for console defaults.
Jordan Lee: Added validation and console warning; updated docs with migration guidance.
